chunks: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not guide you to a weapon that saves you from your enemies and generates your sustenance?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You should supplicate to your Lord by night and by day, for the weapon of the Believer is supplication (du'a).'

key_terms.أَرْزَاق: divinely apportioned sustenance/provision (rizq) — the belief that God controls and distributes all material provision
key_terms.سِلَاحَ الْمُؤْمِنِ: the weapon of the Believer — a famous epithet for du'a emphasizing its protective and empowering function
key_terms.يُنْجِي: to deliver, rescue, or save — used of divine deliverance from danger

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about supplication being the weapon of the believer?
ai.summary: The Prophet (saww) presents du'a (supplication) as the ultimate spiritual weapon available to the believers, promising that it both repels enemies and draws sustenance. This teaching was addressed to the early Muslim community, who faced real physical enemies and material hardship; the Prophet reframed du'a not merely as ritual piety but as active, practical power. The phrase 'weapon of the Believer' (silah al-mu'min) became one of the most quoted expressions in Shia hadith literature concerning the merit of supplication.
